court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Machindra Balasaheb Toke vs Smt. Sneha Machindra Toke
facts_of_case: Parties were married in 2011 and have two children. Husband initiated divorce proceedings under Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act. Wife claimed interim maintenance for herself and children, which was allowed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to disclose material facts can lead to the court drawing adverse inferences.
legal_principles.held: Not only this, it has been specifically mentioned that Respondent is collecting rent receivable from properties which are owned by her parents. She has specifically stated that she has started residing with with her parents.

legal_principles.principle: A party's admission of facts can be used against them.
legal_principles.held: Counsel would urge that Respondent has tendered an affidavit in this Court, thereby admitting the fact that she was investing in mutual funds and share market from 2017 to 2019 from the amount which she has received from her father Pandurang Mane.

legal_principles.principle: The court may draw adverse inferences when a party fails to disclose their income.
legal_principles.held: What can be noticed is, Respondent has not disclosed income from other sources, like the one which is now mentioned in the affidavit before this Court.

outcome.final_order: Trial court order allowing wife's claim for interim maintenance is upheld.
